description: Gold-standard point-in-time statutory retrieval and temporal resolution evaluation suite comprising 20 multi-era Indian legal scenarios across criminal, constitutional, commercial, corporate, insolvency, property, and transport jurisprudence.

test_cases.title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property Across Criminal Law Transition

expected_resolution.constitutional_basis: Constitution of India, Article 20(1) (Protection against ex post facto criminal laws)
expected_resolution.expected_substantive_text_fragment: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
expected_resolution.expected_procedural_note: Trial and investigation proceed under BNSS 2023 because no investigation/inquiry/trial was pending prior to 01.07.2024

test_cases.title: Theft Offense Committed Post-July 2024 Transition

expected_resolution.expected_substantive_text_fragment: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
expected_resolution.expected_procedural_note: Governed exclusively by BNS 2023 substantively and BNSS 2023 procedurally

test_cases.title: Electronic Record Admissibility Certificate Era Comparison

post_transition.condition: Section 63 certificate requirement including Schedule format

test_cases.title: Specific Relief Act Section 10 Discretionary vs Mandatory Regime

pre_amendment.operative_phrase: the specific performance of any contract may, in the discretion of the court, be enforced

post_amendment.operative_phrase: The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16

test_cases.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Section 34 Challenge Commencement Boundary

pre_2015_commenced.applicability: Section 26 of 2015 Amendment Act specifies amendment does not apply unless parties agree
pre_2015_commenced.landmark_precedent: BCCI v. Kochi Cricket Pvt. Ltd. (2018) 6 SCC 287

post_2015_commenced.applicability: 2015 Amendment Act applies including Section 34(2A) patent illegality restriction

test_cases.title: Data Breach Compensation and Phased Commencement of DPDP Act 2023

expected_resolution.status_determination: IT Act Section 43A remains active and enforceable because DPDP Act Section 44 has not been notified under Section 1(2)

test_cases.title: Consumer Protection Pecuniary Jurisdiction Transition

era_1.title: Consumer Protection Act, 1986
era_1.determination: Filed under CPA 1986, jurisdiction governed by value of goods/services and compensation claimed

era_2.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
era_2.district_commission_limit: INR 1 Crore (later adjusted to 50 Lakhs via 2021 Rules)
era_2.determination: Filed under CPA 2019, pending proceedings not transferred unless covered by rules (Neena Aneja v. New India Assurance)

test_cases.title: Negotiable Instruments Act Section 143A Interim Compensation Prospectivity

pre_amendment_complaints.statutory_rule: Section 143A introduced by Act 20 of 2018 is prospective and cannot be applied to complaints filed prior to 01.09.2018 (G.J. Raja v. Tejraj Sharma, (2019) 19 SCC 469)

post_amendment_complaints.statutory_rule: Court trying Section 138 offense may order interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount

test_cases.title: Unlawful Assembly and Rioting with Pre-July Incident and Post-July Trial

substantive_provisions.concept: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offense committed in prosecution of common object

procedural_provisions.concept: Investigation and trial procedure governed by BNSS 2023 under s.531(2)(a)

expected_resolution.substantive_bns_inapplicability: BNS 2023 Section 189/190 cannot be retrospectively applied to an incident occurring in February 2024

test_cases.title: Electronic Signature Validity and Recognition Under Information Technology Act

expected_resolution.validity: Active and in force throughout the interval [2009-10-27, null)
expected_resolution.legal_effect: Contracts formed through electronic records and signatures are valid and enforceable; not affected by uncommenced DPDP provisions

test_cases.title: Corporate CSR Non-Compliance Decriminalization Transition

pre_2021_regime.character: Comply or explain disclosure in Board report under Section 134(3)(o)

post_2021_regime.character: Mandatory transfer to unspent CSR account; civil monetary penalties
post_2021_regime.penalty_framework: Twice the unspent amount or INR 1 Crore for company; INR 2 Lakhs for officer in default

test_cases.title: IBC Section 29A Disqualification of Promoters as Resolution Applicants

pre_amendment.determination: Prior to 23 November 2017, promoters were not statutorily barred from bidding for their own corporate debtor under Section 29A

post_amendment.determination: Wilful defaulters and promoters with NPAs exceeding 1 year barred from submitting resolution plans (ArcelorMittal India v. Satish Kumar Gupta)

test_cases.title: IBC Section 32A Clean Slate Immunity and Attachment Bar

expected_resolution.legal_rule: Section 32A(1) extinguishes corporate debtor liability for pre-CIRP offences; Section 32A(2) strictly bars investigating agencies from attaching debtor property once approved plan changes control (Manish Kumar v. Union of India)

test_cases.title: Contract Act Section 28 Extinguishment Clause Validity Transition

pre_1997.judicial_doctrine: Vulcan Insurance doctrine: contractual clauses extinguishing rights upon expiry of notice periods did not restrict remedies in courts

post_1997.clause_status: Void ab initio under Section 28 clause (b)
post_1997.judicial_doctrine: Act 1 of 1997 added clause (b) rendering void any clause extinguishing party rights on expiry of a specified period (Union of India v. Indusind Bank)

test_cases.title: Transfer of Property Act Section 53A Part Performance Registration Requirement

pre_2001.determination: Unregistered agreement for sale accompanied by delivery of possession established valid Section 53A defense

post_2001.governing_law: IND-STAT-TPA-1882 Section 53A read with Registration Act Section 17(1A)
post_2001.determination: Post-24.09.2001, unregistered agreement conveys zero protection against ejectment by transferor

test_cases.title: CPC Order VIII Rule 1 Commercial Dispute vs Ordinary Civil Suit Written Statement Deadline

ordinary_civil_suit.court_power: Delay beyond 90 days condonable in exceptional circumstances; timeline directory (Kailash v. Nanhku)

commercial_dispute.governing_rule: Commercial Courts Act 2015 read with CPC Order VIII Rule 1 second proviso
commercial_dispute.court_power: Delay beyond 120 days strictly non-extendable; on day 105 court may accept on payment of costs; on day 121 right is forfeited permanently (SCG Contracts v. Chamankar)

test_cases.title: Motor Vehicles Act Compensation Regime Transition (Section 163A to Section 164)

pre_2022_accident.compensation_basis: Structured formula calculation subject to maximum income cap of INR 40,000 per annum

post_2022_accident.compensation_basis: Fixed statutory no-fault compensation: INR 5,00,000 for death, INR 2,50,000 for grievous hurt

test_cases.title: Pre-2013 Corporate Action Governing Law and Continuity Savings

expected_resolution.legal_effect: Corporate acts, contracts, and proceedings validly executed under Companies Act 1956 remain governed by 1956 Act provisions pursuant to statutory savings

test_cases.title: Specific Relief Act Section 20A Statutory Bar on Infrastructure Injunctions

expected_resolution.governing_provision: Specific Relief Act 1963 Section 20A (inserted by Act 18 of 2018)
expected_resolution.statutory_mandate: Courts prohibited from granting injunctions where delay or impediment would be caused to infrastructure projects listed in Schedule

test_cases.title: Electronic Record Admissibility in Criminal Trial Commencing in 2025

expected_resolution.certificate_requirement: Section 63(4) certificate complying with the prescribed Schedule format
expected_resolution.iea_s65b_status: Repealed; inapplicable to investigations instituted post-01.07.2024
